meta.title: From Monday Blindness to Same-Day Store Truth
meta.subtitle: A before-and-after operating week for 120 APAC stores and 2,000 frontline staff

slides.title: From Monday Blindness to Same-Day Store Truth
slides.subtitle: RetailCo operating visibility across 120 stores and 2,000 frontline staff
slides.script: We are starting from the COO week RetailCo described to us: decisions made after the fact, performance trapped inside a few outstanding managers, and onboarding that depends on whoever is rostered that day. The proposal is not a dashboard for its own sake. We are joining Spacesight, Echo, AI Wiki, and Alivia into one operating loop: see the floor, hear the customer conversation, capture the best practice, and turn it into a concrete proposal RetailCo can act on.

slides.title: Where we are taking the conversation
bullets: The cost of the current week
Product mapping to each COO pain
slides.script: We will keep this practical and anchored in the four issues already raised. First, we look at the cost of the current operating rhythm, not by inventing financial figures, but by showing how a blind week behaves across 120 stores. Then we compare today with the week after the new loop is in place. We will map every pain to a named product, including the scheduling issue where we should be honest about what is covered and what needs adjacent work. We finish with one decision for today.

slides.title: The status quo compounds before Monday arrives
slides.label: stores generating last-week truth
slides.note: A Monday spreadsheet turns live store conditions into after-action commentary.
slides.script: We should treat the Monday spreadsheet as more than an inconvenience. Across 120 stores, every trading day creates customer interactions, manager choices, queue patterns, coaching moments, and missed signals. If we only see those signals the following Monday, we are not managing the week; we are reviewing it. That is the cost of the status quo: not a made-up percentage, but a repeated delay between what happens on the floor and what the COO can do about it.

slides.title: The COO week: today versus after

rows.right: Spacesight shows floor activity as it happens
Echo captures customer conversations for scoring
AI Wiki makes winning plays searchable

slides.script: We are reframing the week from retrospective administration to operating awareness. Today, the COO receives a spreadsheet on Monday and has to infer what happened across the estate. With Spacesight, the floor becomes visible closer to the moment of action. With Echo, we do not rely only on sales outcomes; we can hear and score how staff actually speak to customers. With AI Wiki, the good behaviors stop living in individual heads. With Alivia, the pieces become a proposal rather than a pile of tools.

slides.title: Every stated pain has a clear place

rows.right: Echo plus AI Wiki to capture and repeat winning behaviors
AI Wiki for consistent frontline learning and reference
Open item: scheduling workflow, integrations, and ownership
Alivia to turn the operating loop into a client proposal

slides.script: We want to be precise about coverage. The visibility pain maps directly to Spacesight. The three-times performance gap maps to Echo and AI Wiki together, because we need both the real conversations and the place to bottle what works. The six-week onboarding pain maps to AI Wiki, supported by captured examples from the floor. Scheduling is different. None of these products is a roster optimization engine, so we should treat it as an open workstream around workflow, integrations, and team coordination rather than pretending it is solved.

slides.title: Best store versus worst store stops being a mystery

rows.right: Echo identifies what they say differently
AI Wiki stores proven plays for all stores
New hires search the same standard

slides.script: The three-times gap is the clearest signal that RetailCo already has the answer somewhere inside the business. The problem is not that the best store managers are unknowable; it is that their behaviors are not captured in a form other stores can reuse. Echo lets us hear how top performers open, probe, handle objections, and close. AI Wiki then turns those patterns into searchable guidance, so the worst stores are not told to improve in general terms; they can copy specific behaviors from the best.

slides.title: The joined-up operating loop

cards.heading: See
cards.body: Spacesight reveals what happens on the shop floor.

cards.heading: Hear
cards.body: Echo captures and scores customer conversations.

cards.heading: Bottle
cards.body: AI Wiki preserves the best manager playbook.

cards.heading: Propose
cards.body: Alivia turns the loop into an executable proposal.

slides.script: The value comes from the loop, not from isolated point solutions. Spacesight tells us what is happening physically in the store. Echo tells us what is happening verbally between staff and customers. AI Wiki converts the best observed and heard behaviors into a shared operating memory. Alivia then helps package the scope, the sequence, and the rationale into a proposal RetailCo can review and approve. That is how the week changes: the business moves from scattered evidence to a repeatable operating system.

slides.title: Onboarding changes from shadowing to standard practice

rows.right: AI Wiki gives one trusted reference
Best manager examples become reusable content
Echo examples show real customer language

slides.script: The six-week onboarding issue is really a consistency issue. RetailCo is not saying new hires cannot learn; RetailCo is saying the learning experience changes depending on who happens to be working that day. AI Wiki gives every new hire the same place to start and the same source of truth to revisit. Echo adds real examples, so training is not abstract. Store managers still matter, but they coach against a shared standard rather than recreating onboarding from memory every time.

slides.title: The week after today’s decision

steps.label: Day 1
steps.text: Confirm stores, stakeholders, data access, and scheduling workstream owner.

steps.label: Day 2
steps.text: Align Spacesight, Echo, AI Wiki, and Alivia scope.

steps.label: Day 3
steps.text: Define best-manager capture and onboarding content priorities.

steps.label: Day 5
steps.text: Review the first joined-up proposal and open items.

slides.script: If we get the decision today, the following week should be about narrowing ambiguity, not launching a vague transformation. On day one, we agree which stores, stakeholders, and access paths matter, and we name an owner for the scheduling workstream because that is outside the core product coverage. Then we align the product scope, define what best-manager behavior we want to capture first, and decide which onboarding content matters most. By the end of the week, Alivia helps us put the joined-up proposal in front of RetailCo.

slides.title: One decision today
slides.subtitle: Approve the joined-up proposal path for Spacesight, Echo, AI Wiki, and Alivia.
bullets: Separate scheduling as an open workstream
slides.script: We are asking for one decision today: approval to proceed with the joined-up proposal path, rather than treating visibility, conversations, knowledge, and proposal assembly as separate discussions. The week after that decision is concrete. We nominate the executive owner, select the initial stores and stakeholders, confirm data and access requirements, and explicitly separate scheduling as an open workstream with the right RetailCo teams involved. That gives us momentum without overclaiming, and it turns the COO’s Monday problem into an operating design RetailCo can act on.

approach.angle: Lead with the cost of the status quo. Invent no numbers you were not given, but make the reader feel what a week of blind operating costs across the estate.
approach.device: Before-and-after: the COO's week today, then the COO's week with this in place.
approach.opener: Open with a short agenda so the COO knows exactly where you are taking them.
approach.close: Close by asking for one decision today and listing what happens the week after.

structure.label: side titles, comparison tables
